result:
The run is ready for review: the fix and the evidence are pushed, and status.md says READY FOR REVIEW.

**The site's numbers for this cell don't hold up.** No released vLLM (0.32.0 or 0.33.0) or SGLang (0.5.22) can load MiniMax-M3.1-Flash's NVFP4 experts, so the site's competitor numbers can't come from this checkpoint. For a fair comparison I made the same cut (60 layers, 16 of 128 experts) of MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, which has the same architecture and which both competitors load. On it, pie decodes 28% slower than vLLM and 22% slower than SGLang. Pie on the M3.1-Flash cut reproduces the site's own pie number (8.98 vs 8.99 ms).

**Fix** (one commit, `d06613bc4` on `r2g/20261106-0130-b200-x1-minimax-m3-1-flash-decode`): MiniMax's decode attention ran one GPU block per KV head, which is 4 blocks on a 148-SM B200. It now splits each head across a cluster of up to 8 blocks and merges the pieces on-chip. The rule halves the cluster as batches grow, so it stops by 5 rows.

| Workload | Before (ITL p50) | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3.1-Flash, 1 request | 8.976 ms | 8.620 ms | +4.1% decode tok/s |
| M3-MXFP8, 1 request | 9.623 ms | 9.286 ms | +3.6% (vLLM: 28.0% → 25.4% ahead) |
| Concurrency 2 (M3.1-Flash / M3-MXFP8) | | | +1.8% / +2.5% |
| Concurrency 4 (M3.1-Flash / M3-MXFP8) | | | −0.1% / +1.7% |
| Concurrency 8–64, prefill batches | | | unchanged within run-to-run noise |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next mini | 0.850 ms | 0.822 ms | +3.4% |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.029 ms | 1.028 ms | unchanged, identical tokens |

All speed numbers are medians of 3 rounds at the full SM clock (1965 MHz).

**Numerics:**
- **M3-MXFP8:** greedy tokens are identical (8 requests × 256 tokens).
- **M3.1-Flash:** tokens first differ at token 1–8 on 6 of 8 requests. At the three divergences I measured, the top two logits were within bf16 rounding of each other.
- **Logit comparison:** I compared logits position by position over a fixed token sequence (teacher-forced), against pie's existing scalar attention path as a reference that is already accepted. The fix moves logits less than that path on all 8 requests checked.

**Tests:**
- **New test:** at MiniMax's shape, so every block of the cluster holds keys; a deliberately broken merge fails it.
- **GPU suite on the final commit:** engine-cuda passed 69/69, 58/59 and 5/6; kernels-cuda passed 34/35 and 142/144.
- **Failures:** all five also fail on main with the same messages.
- **CI check:** `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.

**Not shipped (attribution in report.md):**
- **Query/key norm + RoPE + cache write:** the biggest remaining item, about 0.7 ms per step. It runs as two single-block kernels. A reverted prototype using a hand-written kernel bought about 4% more, but CUDA retired that kernel's fusion rule on purpose, so the proper fix is deeper compiler/kernel work.
- **Expert-layer glue and the NVFP4 expert GEMM:** each is more than about 3 hours of kernel work.

**Side findings:**
- **bf16 by default:** pie serves both cuts as bf16 by default, and on this pod the bf16 load runs out of host memory. Written up separately in `identify-bug.md` with file and line references. To measure the real precision I edited `~/.pie/models/minimax_m3.poem` on the pod, and that edit is still in place.
- **Dense first layers:** pie runs M3.1-Flash's first three layers as dense attention although the model's config uses sparse attention there. The output is the same at this context length but would differ past 2048 tokens.
- **Site parameter count:** the site's 124.25 B parameter figure doesn't match a 16-expert cut, which counts to 64.67 B.

An independent review found two blockers (formatting, and a test that never exercised the merge with more than one block) plus several number and wording errors. All are fixed, and that round also tightened the cluster rule after the first version lost 1% at concurrency 8.

Everything is in `/root/r2g/evidence`; open `report.md` and `pr.md` first.
